content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge resolves the Matthew 1:16 link by treating its own wording as admitting both readings, rather than weighing the pressed chain against the defender's chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'never verse by verse' can be read as merely forbidding an isolated contrary-state test or as forbidding using a single verse's ambiguity to declare the link underdetermined; I weighed those two readings.","why":"The judge's sole stated reason is that Matthew 1:16's wording admits both readings, which is a verse-by-verse stating-verse analysis rather than the chain-by-chain footing K-C requires."}
